text:
Chandler Stephenson has two Stanley Cup rings, one from Washington in 2018 and one from Vegas in 2023, and a big role in Seattle: 17:37 a night at center, plenty of power-play time. Fourteen points in 23 games, twelve of them assists, six on the power play.

The trouble is everything else. Seattle has only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five when he is out there, eight points worse than when he sits, and that is not new: Evolving-Hockey had opponents gaining more with him on the ice than with almost any forward in the league last season. His own shooting has nearly disappeared, 19 shots in 23 games and 0.29 expected goals per 60 minutes, down from 0.40.

There is a little bad luck in the mix. Seattle has scored 5.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on, and Evolving-Hockey noted his teammates were among the weakest of any forward. But three points in his last ten games with no goals is the form line, and the Kraken's top line now runs through Matty Beniers. Watch how long Stephenson keeps those minutes.
